{{Quote|Endurance and concentration are the key words here, and the total utilization of our neural-cranial synapses is absolutely essential.|Dromboid|audio=Dromboid-Endurance.flac|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
'''Dromboid''' was an [[Amorphiian]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who worked for an [[Unidentified Amorphiian company|Amorphiian company]] that distributed technologies around [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. He hosted an [[instruction cassette]] video that accompanied a brand of [[mini-transmitter]] sold outside the company's base in the [[Amorphiia system/Legends|Amorphiia system]].

On [[Life Day/Legends|Life Day]] in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], [[Lumpawaroo/Legends|Lumpawarrump]], a [[Youngling/Legends|young]] [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], attempted to assemble a [[Transmitter/Legends|mini-transmitter]] by viewing its instruction cassette. However, because Dromboid suffered from the power fluctuations typical of his [[Species/Legends|species]], the methodical and often-interrupted instructions frustrated the Wookiee as much as they helped him.

A fastidious representative of his species, Dromboid spoke with an even and emotionless keel, yet purported to appreciate beauty. Although his malfunctions often impaired his motor abilities, the Amorphiian taught with efficiency and never acknowledged his failures.

==Biography==
===Amorphiian representative===
{{Quote|Thank you for selecting our brand of mini-transmitter. If you assemble it properly, following the instructions I am about to give you, it will provide many years of fun, and valuable service to you.|Dromboid|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
[[File:Lumpy-Dromboid-HS.png|thumb|right|225px|Lumpawarrump watches Dromboid's video.]]
Dromboid<ref name="Insider">{{InsiderCite|106|I Have a Bad Feeling About This!}}</ref> was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] citizen of<ref name="SWHS" /> the [[Eidoloni sector/Legends|Eidoloni sector]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Atlas">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Amorphiia system/Legends|Amorphiia system]]</ref> [[Amorphiia]] who represented a [[Unidentified Amorphiian company|company]] based in the [[Amorphiia system/Legends|Amorphiia system]]. The company sold various technologies throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], one such product being a model of [[mini-transmitter]].<ref name="SWHS" />

On [[Life Day/Legends|Life Day]] in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=870#15778940|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2006-10-12|time=6:13 PM|quote=Wookiee Life Day occurs every 3 years, one of which fell at ~1.5 ABY.}}</ref> the [[Youngling/Legends|young]] [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Lumpawaroo/Legends|Lumpawarrump]] from the planet [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] acquired an unassembled [[Transmitter/Legends|mini-transmitter]] from the [[Amorphiian]] company. The package included an [[instruction cassette]] video hosted by Dromboid.<ref name="SWHS" />

===Assembling the mini-transmitter===
====Unconventional instructor====
{{Quote|But now, let's get started, shall we? First, find the sealed package containing all the tools you'll need. [&hellip;] It looks like this. Try not to rip it open, because it makes a very handy storage case for your tools until you need them again. Now, this is the first thing you'll need. Please be careful not to hurt yourself on the sharp edges. Ouch.|Dromboid, beginning the assembly|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
In the video, Dromboid&mdash;holding a mini-transmitter&mdash;thanked the viewers for selecting the Amorphiian brand, assuring that the mini-transmitter would provide many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of fun and valuable service, given that the product was assembled properly. As the Amorphiian finished his introduction, the [[Limb/Legends|forefinger]] of his right hand went limp due to a power loss, and he nudged it back to life with his [[Nose/Legends|nose]] before continuing. Flipping switches on the mini-transmitter and preparing to begin, Dromboid lost power to his left leg, so, twitching, he patted it back into motion.<ref name="SWHS" />

[[File:Dromboid-smile.png|thumb|left|225px|Dromboid loosens his smile.]]
Setting the mini-transmitter on a table, he began searching for the tools necessary for the assembly. As he reached for the small, clear [[Plastic/Legends|plastic]] bag containing the instruments, the Amorphiian's elbows locked at a closed angle, so, embarrassed, he began to flap his bent arms to unlock the joints. Arms again working, Dromboid picked up the sealed bag, which he suggested not to rip, as it would be useful for storage.<ref name="SWHS" />

Removing a [[Screwdriver/Legends|screwdriver]]-like tool, the Amorphiian warned the viewers about its sharp edges, demonstrating the danger by pretending to prick his finger, saying "ouch," and smiling. However, Dromboid's mouth became stuck in the smiling position, so he twisted the tool underneath his chin, readjusting his smile and producing a popping sound when done.<ref name="SWHS" />

====Technical difficulties====
{{Quote|Now, watch me closely&hellip; I'm going to assemble our mini-transmitters together. Let us work slowly and methodically because this is a&hellip;job worth&hellip;doing well.|Dromboid, suffering from a power failure|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
Next, Dromboid picked up a [[circuit-breaker module]], insisting the use of its proper name. While emphasizing the word "module," his mouth froze, so Dromboid rapidly clicked his [[Tongue/Legends|tongue]] and rubbed his forehead to reactivate his [[Language/Legends|speech]]. Operational once again, the Amorphiian reminded the viewers that all ten thousand of the circuit-breaker module's terminals must be paired with wires of corresponding [[Color/Legends|colors]]. As he began to demonstrate the build, Dromboid's [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] temporarily crossed and drifted upwards, and the instructor then recommended that the assembly be done slowly and methodically.<ref name="SWHS" />

Running out of [[Time/Legends|time]] left in the video, Dromboid began the complicated assembly of the [[impulse-to-voice translator]], a component he described to be the [[Heart/Legends|heart]] of the mini-transmitter, as it was responsible for converting the electronic energy into a recognizable language. Noting that viewers should stay alert for the procedure, the Amorphiian expressed the importance of endurance and concentration to utilize the full capacity of their [[Brain/Legends|brains]]. As Dromboid finished speaking, he suffered another power fluctuation, making him collapse down to the table, place a finger to his nose, and fall to the floor.<ref name="SWHS" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Re-remember, every one of the ten thousand terminals on your circuit-breaker module is marked in a particular color. Beautiful, aren't they? Like a rainbow.|Dromboid stutters as he admires a circuit-breaker module|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
[[File:Dromboid-forehead-HS.png|thumb|right|225px|Dromboid, reactivating his speech]]
A male member of the [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] Amorphiian [[Species/Legends|species]], Dromboid had light-colored skin, blue eyes, and gray [[Hair/Legends|hair]]. Due to his Amorphiian physiology, Dromboid often suffered from power losses that impaired his motor abilities. The malfunctions had a variety of consequences, including the freezing of joints and muscles, voice alterations, and whirring noises.<ref name="SWHS" />

Although they would spontaneously interrupt his speech or actions,<ref name="SWHS" /> Dromboid corrected his impairments<ref name="Script">{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsholidayspecial.com/text/swhs_script-fourth_draft.pdf|text=The Fourth Draft Script - 09/13/78|work=[http://www.starwarsholidayspecial.com The Star Wars Holiday Special]|archivedate=20170909041232}}</ref> by various means, such as cranking his arms, nudging his nose, clicking his tongue, and rubbing his forehead. Throughout the instruction cassette owned by Lumpawarrump, Dromboid was halted by numerous power fluctuations,<ref name="SWHS" /> which frustrated the young, anxious Wookiee.<ref name="Script" />

Despite his breakdowns, Dromboid was a smart and efficient instructor. Whenever power failures occurred, he would make no mention of them, simply correcting the problem and resuming his speech or action.<ref name="Script" /> The Amorphiian also practiced a methodical work ethic, believing that doing a job well was worth the extra time.<ref name="SWHS" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|Now find the circuit-breaker module. And by the way, let's start calling these components by their proper names. 'Circuit-breaker module.'|Dromboid|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
As the host of the mini-transmitter instruction cassette, Dromboid guided viewers through the different tools and components&mdash;most notably the circuit-breaker module and the impulse-to-voice translator. In the cassette, the Amorphiian wore a white, collared [[shirt]] under a tan, dark-trimmed [[Jacket/Legends|jacket]]. Over the jacket was a large-buckled [[Belt/Legends|belt]], which was matched with a pair of black pants.<ref name="SWHS" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Harvey Korman, as Dromboid, appears on the screen, as a kind of Milton Cross/Bergen Evans instructor, who is guiding the youngster[s] of the galaxy through the mysteries of electronics&hellip;He is knowledgeable, efficient, and intelligent&mdash;but of a race which has the physical oddity of losing power from time to time in various parts of the body. When this happens, he makes no mention of it, nor even a comment of any sort. He just gets that part working again, and continues whatever he was doing or saying.|''The Star Wars Holiday Special'' script, fourth draft|<ref name="Script" />}}
[[File:HarveyKorman.png|thumb|right|150px|Harvey Korman portrayed Dromboid in ''The Star Wars Holiday Special''.]]
The character of Dromboid was created for ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'',<ref name="SWHS" /> a television film that aired on [[CBS]] in the [[Wikipedia:United States|United States]] on [[November 17]], [[1978]], for the first and only time.<ref name="Cantina">{{SW|url=news/the-star-wars-holiday-special-cantina-we-may-not-thrive-friend-but-we-survive-friend|text=''The Star Wars Holiday Special'' Cantina: Who's Who|int=The Star Wars Holiday Special Cantina: Who's Who|nolive=1}}</ref> In the ''Holiday Special'', Dromboid appears in a four-minute-long comedy sketch preceding a commercial break. In the scene, Dromboid is portrayed by comedic guest star [[Harvey Korman]]<ref name="SWHS" /> who also played the character [[Gormaanda/Legends|Gormaanda]] in a prior sketch and the character [[Krelman]] in the following one.<ref name="SWHS" />

The purposed humor of Dromboid's scene, referred to in the script as the "Harvey Korman 'Dromboid' segment," is that his constant malfunctions prevent him from giving timely instructions to Lumpawarrump, which angers the young, eager Wookiee.<ref name="Script" /> To accomplish the filming of these malfunctions, clips of Korman were edited to create stutters, spasms, and vocal changes.<ref name="SWHS" /> The ''Holiday Special''{{'s}} fourth draft compares Dromboid's demeanor to those of [[Wikipedia:Milton Cross|Milton Cross]] and [[Wikipedia:Bergen Evans|Bergen Evans]],<ref name="Script" /> a radio announcer<ref name="Cross">{{Blogspot|subdomain=tenwatts|url=2007/12/milton-cross.html|name=ARCADE RADIO TRIVIA|text=A Milton Cross Christmas|date=2007-12-28}}</ref> and educational television host, respectively.<ref name="Evans">{{WebCite|url=http://www.peabodyawards.com/award-profile/the-last-word|text=The Last Word|work=[http://www.peabodyawards.com The Peabody Awards]|archivedate=20170829022704}}</ref> However, in the time since the film aired, Dromboid's quirky behavior has been likened to that of [[Wikipedia:Max Headroom (character)|Max Headroom]], the erratic titular character of [[Wikipedia:The Max Headroom Show|''The Max Headroom Show'']], a comedy talk show that aired nearly a decade later.<ref name="Sci-Fi">{{WebCite|url=https://unobtainium13.com/2015/12/15/film-review-the-star-wars-holiday-special-1978-dir-steve-binder-david-acomba|text=Sci-Fi Review: The Star Wars Holiday Special (1978, dir. Steve Binder & David Acomba)|author=Troutman, Valerie|date=2015-12-15|work=[https://unobtainium13.com Through the Shattered Lens]|archivedate=20170829022825}}</ref>

Although Dromboid is not identified by name in the film,<ref name="SWHS" /> the name is used throughout the ''Holiday Special''{{'s}} fourth-draft script.<ref name="Script" /> The name Dromboid was later confirmed as [[canon]] within the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity by [[Alex Newborn]]'s [[2008]] article, "[[I Have a Bad Feeling About This!]]," published in the [[Star Wars Insider 106|106th issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine.<ref name="Insider" />
